sections.title: What a marketing agency invoice must show
sections.body: A good agency invoice prevents client questions. You must clearly separate your management fee from the actual ad spend. Mixing these two creates accounting headaches and makes your agency look artificially expensive. Always list your monthly retainer fee as an advance payment for the upcoming month. For project work, detail the specific deliverables completed. If the client requested extra revisions or new assets, list these as approved out-of-scope changes. Include the original quote reference and the exact date the work was approved. This clarity speeds up the payment process.
items: Separate management fees from ad spend

sections.title: How marketing agencies price and bill work
sections.body: Marketing agencies typically use three pricing models. Monthly retainers cover ongoing work like social media management or SEO. You bill these in advance on the first of the month. Project fees cover fixed deliverables like a website build or a branding package. You usually split these into a deposit and milestone payments. Finally, agencies handle ad spend. Never mark up the ad spend directly on the invoice without a clear management fee line. Clients need to know exactly how much money goes to the ad network versus your agency.
items: Never hide fees in ad spend

sections.title: Getting paid: terms, deposits and chasing
sections.body: Cash flow is critical for a marketing agency. Always collect a deposit before starting a fixed project. A standard deposit is fifty percent upfront. For monthly retainers, enforce strict payment terms. If a client fails to pay their retainer invoice by the fifth of the month, pause the ad campaigns and stop work. Clearly state these terms on every invoice. Use our free invoice generator at /tools/free-invoice-generator to add custom payment terms to your PDFs. Send polite payment reminders a few days before the due date to avoid late payments.

faqs.q: Should I include ad spend on my agency invoice?
faqs.a: It is best practice to have the client pay the ad network directly using their own credit card. If you must bill for ad spend, list it as a completely separate line item from your management fee. Mixing them inflates your revenue artificially and confuses the client about your actual costs.

faqs.q: When should I invoice for a monthly retainer?
faqs.a: Always invoice for a monthly retainer in advance. Send the invoice a few days before the new month begins, with payment due on the first. This ensures you have the funds secured before your team dedicates hours to the client. Working without upfront payment on retainers puts your agency at risk.

faqs.q: How do I bill for out-of-scope marketing work?
faqs.a: Get written approval for any extra work before you begin. Once approved, add the extra work to your next invoice as a distinct line item. Label it clearly as an approved change request so the client remembers authorising the extra cost. This prevents disputes and ensures you are compensated fairly.
